messages:
maya: Heads-up — we just got an alert: large number of gpu pods pending in eu-west-1 and a weird HPA surge. Cost jump on infra billing dashboard.

sam: seeing the same. HPA metric looks like `qps_per_pod` but it's computed from an egress latency histogram + request count aggregate. It spikes when egress gets throttled by the region quota.

jordan: can you paste the alert?

maya: alert: GPU-Pods-Pending > 50 for 3m. NodePool eu-gpu-prod at max-size. HPA target replicas jumped from 60->420 then CA tried to provision nodes but hit regional egress quota causing nodes stuck in provisioning -> pods pending.

lee: ohhh. so HPA reacts to an application-level proxy metric that correlates with network egress congestion. When egress borks, latency rises and HPA scales up, CA asks for more GPU nodes, but quota prevents node create, leading to pending pods and cost anomalies.

sam: exact sequence. Also see a bunch of evicted pods because kubelet OOMKilled some sidecar memory during the scramble. Evictions freed up some slots which briefly lowered the metric, HPA then scaled down, and we got a thrash.

maya: infra-bot shows many CA events: `FailedCreate: quota exceeded: InsufficientEgressQuota` and `NodeProvisionTimeout`.

infra-bot: CA events (eu-west-1): FailedCreate (egress quota), ProvisioningTimeouts x12, NodeGroupScalingRequestBlocked.

jordan: short-term mitigations: 1) cap HPA max replicas for this service to avoid runaway. 2) add a floor on the HPA so we don't oscillate to zero. 3) change the HPA metric to `queue_length` instead of raw egress latency.

lee: agree. Also we should: annotate the CA NodeGroup with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: "true"`? Maybe not — we don't want permanently disabled. Better: increase CA max nodes and request quota from cloud for eu-west region, or provision a small warm GPU pool (tainted) that can absorb spike.

sam: action plan I'm going to implement now: reduce HPA.maxReplicas to 120, switch metric to `custom.prometheus/requests_in_queue` (server-side rate limited), and add stabilization window of 5m.

maya: paste the HPA change snippet?

sam: ````
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: gpu-worker-hpa
spec:
  minReplicas: 10
  maxReplicas: 120
  metrics:
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: requests_in_queue
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "50"
  behaviour:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30
      policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 100
        periodSeconds: 60
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
````

jordan: nice. Also add the annotation to the deployment to prefer nodes from warm pool: `node.kubernetes.io/tier: warm-gpu` and taint the warm pool with `dedicated=warm:NoSchedule` then have deployment tolerations. That reduces coldstart.

lee: I created a 4-node warm pool (tainted) in eu-west-1 and updated the nodeSelector for a canary deployment. If this looks ok, we can keep it as a small buffer while cloud quota request goes through.

maya: will that blow up cost? small bump but better than provisioning storm + failed nodes. We already burned credits from failed attempts.

sam: long term: 1) move metric away from egress-proxied latency. 2) Add a smoothing rollup in Prometheus for the custom metric (increase scrape step and use rate(window)). 3) adjust CA settings: `--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m` and `--max-node-provision-time=15m` to avoid aggressive churn. 4) add a pre-check in the controller that maps HPA desires to available quota and caps requests.

jordan: reminder — VPA is currently in "off" for this deployment. If we enable VPA in "auto" it will change requests on pods which will cause CA to churn because requests affect scheduling decisions. So prefer request-preserving autoscaling (only adjust limits or use recommender for human review).

lee: I'm opening a cloud support ticket to increase regional egress quota and requesting temporary burst quota. Ticket ID: CS-9042. ETA ~48h.

maya: for incident timeline & postmortem: please log what HPA decided, CA events, and invoice delta. I'll start an incident doc.

sam: done — HPA patched and pushed to canary. Monitoring: watching `pod_pending_count`, `ca_events`, `gpu_node_provision_errors`, and billing delta.

infra-bot: monitor rule created: watch eu-west GPU pending > 10 for 10m -> notify #eng-infra and trigger runbook.

maya: thanks everyone. follow-ups: - jordan to update runbook with warm-pool pattern - lee to update cloud ticket with exact node template - sam to roll HPA change to prod if canary stable for 30m.

lee: noted. will also add a short-lived `--expander=random` test on ca to avoid a single group saturation.

jordan: one more: add a PodDisruptionBudget to avoid mass evictions during churn. example:
```
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: gpu-workers-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gpu-worker
```

maya: ok closing thread when prod stable. thanks team :thumbsup:
